connection.notInstalledBody: PartBuddy shows and changes designs through SolidCraft, a free CAD program. Install SolidCraft, then look again.
connection.notRunningBody: Start SolidCraft here, or open it yourself; PartBuddy finds it on its own.
connection.startingBody: SolidCraft is starting without a window of its own: PartBuddy shows the model itself. This usually takes a moment.
connection.lostTitle: The connection to SolidCraft was lost
connection.lostBody: PartBuddy keeps the last model and connects again as soon as SolidCraft answers.
connection.emptyBody: Create a body in SolidCraft or let the assistant design one. It appears here after every step.
connection.mirrorFailedTitle: The model could not be mirrored
connection.mirrorFailedBody: PartBuddy shows the last good state. Details: {detail}
connection.emptyBodyHeadless: Tell the assistant what you need. Every step appears here, sketches even before the body.

print.chipHint: Change the material of this part and the printer
print.materialFailed: The material could not be set.
print.name: Name
print.printerHint: The highlighted printer is in use. Walls under two line widths print poorly; the assistant is told.
print.materialHint: Starting values for a common printer. Adjust them to your test prints; the assistant builds with these clearances.
print.saveFailed: The profiles could not be saved.
print.supportFreeHint: The assistant chamfers edges facing the bed instead of rounding them, gives wide lying holes a teardrop roof and bridges countersinks that open downwards, so the slicer needs no support.

check.title: Ready to print?
check.none: Nothing found: the part fits the build volume, the walls are thick enough, nothing needs support.
check.basis: Checked after every change, in the print orientation below, with the printer and material of this part.

finding.size: Too large for the build volume: {size} mm, the printer takes {bed} mm
finding.sizeLying: Too large for the build volume: {size} mm, the printer takes {bed} mm. Laid on another side it would fit.
finding.wallTooThin: Walls only {thickness} mm, thinner than the nozzle ({nozzle} mm): they do not print
finding.wallThin: Walls only {thickness} mm, at least {minimum} mm (two lines)
finding.supportFillet: {area} mm² of rounded edges facing the bed lean beyond {limit}° and need support
finding.supportHole: {area} mm² on top of lying holes too wide to bridge need support
finding.supportRibs: {area} mm² that need support stand on support walls printed into the model: turn the slicer's supports off
finding.supportCounterbore: {area} mm² of counterbore steps facing the bed: the hole cuts the bridge over them, so they need support
finding.contact: Only {area} mm² lie on the bed: may come loose or tip over
finding.separate: {bodies} touch but are separate bodies: the slicer lays each on the bed by itself. Combine them if they are one part.

confirm.title: Export anyway?
confirm.body: The print check is red. As it is, the part will likely not print cleanly:

try.roof: {count, plural, one {Give the hole a roof} other {Give the # holes a roof}}
try.bridge: {count, plural, one {Bridge the counterbore in steps} other {Bridge the # counterbores in steps}}
try.ribs: {count, plural, one {Print a support wall into the model} other {Print # support walls into the model}}

preview.chamfer: The ghost shows chamfers of the same size at 45°: they print without support.
preview.roof: The ghost shows the roof: 45° flanks, flat on top where the slicer bridges it.
preview.bridge: The ghost shows the stepped bridge: one layer with a slot as wide as the hole, one with a square. The slicer bridges both from wall to wall.
preview.ribs: The ghost shows the walls: 1 mm thick, 4 mm apart, one layer below the part and 0.5 mm off its sides. They break off after printing; turn the slicer's supports off.

fix.refused: SolidCraft cannot do it this way: {detail}

done.chamfer: The rounds facing the bed are chamfers now.
done.roof: {count, plural, one {The hole has a roof now.} other {The # holes have a roof now.}}
done.bridge: {count, plural, one {The counterbore is bridged in steps now.} other {The # counterbores are bridged in steps now.}}
done.ribs: {count, plural, one {A support wall is printed into the model now.} other {# support walls are printed into the model now.}}

request.chamfer: Make the rounded edges facing the bed ({faces}) 45° chamfers of the same size, so they print without support.
request.roof: Give the lying holes ({faces}) a 45° teardrop roof, flat on top where the slicer can bridge it, so nothing leans more than {limit}°.
request.bridge: Add a stepped bridge over the counterbore steps facing the bed ({faces}): one layer with a slot as wide as the hole across the bore, one with a square, so they print without support.
request.ribs: Print breakaway support walls into the model under the overhangs ({faces}): separate bodies named "Print support", 1 mm thick, 4 mm apart, standing on the bed, one layer below the part and 0.5 mm off its sides.

orientation.title: Print orientation
orientation.numbers: Support {support} mm² · on the bed {contact} mm² · height {height} mm
orientation.tooLarge: Does not fit the build volume this way
orientation.loadSlanted: Load at an angle to the layers
orientation.loads: {count, plural, one {Load marked on # face} other {Load marked on # faces}}
orientation.loadHint: Does a force act on the part? Select a face and “Load acts here”, and the proposal lays the layers to suit.
orientation.laid: Now lying on {face}. 3MF and STL are exported this way.
orientation.failed: The print orientation could not be saved.

fit.targetHole: Hole Ø{target} mm = {mating} + 2 × {clearance} clearance + {shrink} hole allowance ({material})
fit.direct: Directly through {label}, preview in the view
fit.viaAssistant: No single parameter drives it: the assistant does it
fit.requestHole: Make {name} a hole with a “{fit}” fit for a Ø{mating} mm counterpart: Ø{target} mm ({clearance} mm clearance per side and {shrink} mm hole allowance for {material}). Keep the nominal size and the clearance as their own parameters and leave the rest of the part as it is.
fit.requestPin: Make {name} a pin with a “{fit}” fit for a hole that prints at Ø{mating} mm: Ø{target} mm ({clearance} mm clearance per side, {material}). Keep the nominal size and the clearance as their own parameters and leave the rest of the part as it is.
fit.targetPinGrowth: Pin Ø{target} mm = {mating} − 2 × {clearance} clearance − {growth} measured growth ({material})

measure.intro: Measurements after printing for {material}. Choose another material in the “Material” tab. From the measurements PartBuddy suggests the hole allowance, outer growth and clearances.
measure.invalid: Enter drawn and measured as numbers in mm.
measure.failed: The measurement could not be saved.
measure.suggestHole: Hole allowance {from} → {to} mm ({count, plural, one {from # measurement} other {median of # measurements}})
measure.suggestOuter: Outer growth {from} → {to} mm ({count, plural, one {from # measurement} other {median of # measurements}})
measure.noSuggestion: The measurements match the current values.
